newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cereals officials to discuss modified maize.
newsitem.headline: EU cereals officials to discuss modified maize.

text.p: European Union cereals officials will on Thursday exchange views on genetically modified maize, an EU official said on Wednesday.
"There will be no decision but the cereals management committee (is) being asked to discuss the issue," the official said.
Three scientific and expert groups are due to report in December on whether there is a risk to health in allowing the import of genetically modified maize.
The European Commission has already allowed member states individually to import genetically modified soybean but shipments have been subject to protests by Greenpeace.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has said he will await the findings of the expert groups before making a recommendation to the Commission on genetically modified maize.
Cereals officials will also discuss national aids to the EU food aid scheme and will set refunds for food aid for December.
"There will be a general discussion on national aids and a vote is expected setting refunds for December," the official said.
Rice experts will discuss the rice market situation and aids for the supply of rice to peripheral regions. "There will be
a discussion and a possible vote on aid for the supply of rice to peripheral regions of the Union," the official said
The committee will on Thursday amend the draft regulation on aid for the supply of rice to the so-called Poseidom countries.
"The draft regulation (980/92) covering supplies to Guyana, Martinique and Guadaloupe was postponed last week and is now expected to be set at Thursday's meeting," the official said.
The committee will also vote on detailed rules on compensatory aid for rice producers.

"Under the reform of the rice regime their is to be a gradual reduction in the intervention price for rice. EU producers will get area compensatory payments similar to those which apply in the cereals sector," the official said.
The first area payments are due to be issued for the 1997/98 marketing year next year.
Rice experts postponed discussion last week but are now expected to reach agreement before the management committee vote.
The committee will open a special export tender for 100,000 tonnes of maize from northern Greece.

"The committee is expected to decide this item left over from the previous week and it will also open two annual tenders for manioc from Thailand and from other third countries as well as for sweet potatoes and for manioc starch," the official said.
